a:

just for completeness sake - it is possible to say "in front of" but not "in front of". for example, you could say "i am in front of your book". but you cannot say "in front of your book" as far as i know. i could be wrong though. but you can use "in front of" to indicate "at least with a little effort" that the object is in front of a reference.
